title: Martine — CPC and CPC Plus graphics converter

Modern converter with OCP Art Studio/Impdraw-compatible output and its own pixel packing implementation. Classified as tooling; CPC graphics conversion and asset preparation. title: mzm2met — embedded NES ROM extraction
reason: Implemented bounded ROM decompressor/extractor with version-specific recipes mzm2met() decompresses headerless SZS data, apply_lzss_ofss() patches LZSS-compressed regions, and the output explicitly receives an iNES header. README gives offsets and input hashes for three 8 MiB MZM variants. Tool execution requires the user-supplied source image and correct per-version ranges. Primary documentation uses the acronym MZM rather than a full commercial title; the record does not expand it or assert an unsupported source-host machine. Version/offset-specific extraction is not an engine reconstruction or game-specific emulation runtime. Code has bounds checks but no independently verified output hash. MIT applies to tool code only. Supplied ROM recipes do not grant input or extracted-game redistribution rights.

title: volamos — AmigaOS CLI compatibility runtime

No Kickstart ROM is needed for normal use. It is generic development/analysis tooling, not a native reconstruction of a specific game; graphics, custom chips, Workbench GUI and games are explicitly out of scope. Linux/macOS build and guest execution are corroborated by current CI logs; published Windows x86-64 binaries compile but Windows/Wine runtime remains unverified. Interpreter/JIT parity covers six fixtures; comparison with vamos includes three documented known divergences, so it is not universal compatibility proof.

title: BlueVessel — native C64 raster-effects intro

README documents both PAL and 65-cycle NTSC operation and describes the implementation in detail. Upstream explicitly says old 64-cycle NTSC does not work and notes a half-cycle visual artifact on WinVICE 3.x; do not generalize to all C64 video models. Code comment says Jeroen Tel granted permission to use Noisy Pillars in this intro; that is not a general music-relicensing grant.

title: T-Rex 64 — native C64 dinosaur-runner recreation

README documents real C64 and VICE execution; release notes report NTSC, SID-filter and real-hardware fixes. Release-note and build claims remain upstream reports, not independently reproduced results. MIT license was inspected for repository code; the recreation’s recognizable game concept and any third-party music derivation should not be treated as unrestricted original IP.

title: ZZ9000 — native AmigaOS driver suite
reason: Network device.c implements native SANA-II Amiga driver dispatch and hardware access; rtg/mntgfx-gcc.c implements graphics-card integration. README identifies the original MNT source and independent fork status, with firmware and ARM-side logic in separate repositories. Top-level build invokes pinned Amiga toolchain workflows; net/Makefile sets68020 and includes host-side test targets elsewhere in the suite. A reviewed code-fix commit explicitly credits Codex review; attribution is limited to review assistance. Requires ZZ9000 ZorroII/III hardware; ZZ9000AX audio and Picasso96/USB/network dependencies vary by component. Matched firmware/bitstream/SDK versions matter, especially ZorroII memory-layout negotiation; driver source alone does not provide a complete setup. The board’s ARM coprocessors are not the CPU executing the Amiga-side network driver; retain separate roles. No independent hardware/runtime/test execution; original MNT lineage is one family, not an extra project count.
